players.product: data-center chillers, BASX custom air handlers & liquid-cooling packages (Redmond / Memphis)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results (CFO): net sales increased 54% year-over-year to a record $496.9 million, driven by both BASX and AAON brands; gross margin was 25.1%, down 170 basis points from 26.8%; non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA increased 44% to $78 million; diluted EPS was $0.48, up 37%. CEO: the sixth consecutive quarter of record backlog.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales $496.9 million (+54% YoY); gross margin 25.1%; adjusted EBITDA $78 million (+44%); diluted EPS $0.48 (+37%)

quarterly_data.signal: BASX (data-center cooling) demand remained exceptionally strong: BASX-branded sales grew 72% year-over-year against a lofty comparison, with all three facilities (Longview, Memphis, Redmond) delivering record BASX-branded sales. BASX posted a book-to-bill ratio over two; record BASX-branded backlog was up 24% sequentially. Management says the data center thermal management market is growing at approximately 30%, so BASX revenue and order growth imply continued share gains.
quarterly_data.figure: BASX-branded sales +72% YoY; BASX book-to-bill over two; BASX-branded backlog +24% sequentially

quarterly_data.signal: Segment detail (CFO): AAON Coil Products sales were $117.6 million (+25%), driven by $93.2 million in BASX branded liquid cooling product sales, which increased 40%; Coil Products gross margin was 24.1%, up 280 basis points sequentially on higher Longview throughput and BASX mix. BASX segment sales grew 104% to $135.4 million at a 23.9% gross margin, with increased Memphis utilization a significant factor; BASX segment sales and margins are expected to expand through the year, second half weighted more favorably.
quarterly_data.figure: BASX branded liquid cooling product sales $93.2 million (+40%); BASX segment sales $135.4 million (+104%), gross margin 23.9%; Coil Products sales $117.6 million

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 outlook raised to sales growth of 40%-45% at a gross margin of 27%-28% (higher growth, more modest near-term margins). CEO: the new 40%-45% top-line marker implies roughly $1 billion in BASX revenue for the year, with AAON-branded sales not markedly different from the prior plan. BASX acceleration came from choosing to accelerate the production ramp (partly via outsourcing) to capture strong data center demand from existing and new customers.
quarterly_data.figure: roughly $1 billion in BASX revenue for the year (implied by 40%-45% sales growth guide)

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center capacity: CEO says prior 'rough napkin math' put BASX capacity at about $1.5 billion, but the initial investments in Longview and Memphis embed more revenue potential, 'being above $2 billion for sure'; the big lifts are already embedded in investments made, with only sequential equipment additions needed. Memphis contribution stepped up from Q4 to Q1 and is expected to grow sequentially through 2026 as the operation matures.
quarterly_data.figure: BASX capacity above $2 billion (vs earlier about $1.5 billion)

quarterly_data.signal: Capex: Q1 capital expenditures totaled $52.9 million for incremental capacity; CFO confirms $190 million remains the full-year 2026 expectation, heavily concentrated on building out Memphis. Q1 operating cash flow was +$34 million, the highest since Q3 2024; debt $425.2 million, leverage ratio 1.71x.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 capex $52.9 million; 2026 capex $190 million; operating cash flow +$34 million

quarterly_data.signal: Supply/capacity constraints: gross margin was hit by increased outsourced components to drive growth, unabsorbed fixed costs at the new Memphis facility, and tariff/inflation pressures, all described as temporary. Longview coil capacity was tied up supporting BASX liquid cooling products, so more outsourcing was done for Oklahoma; coils are being outsourced short-term as a hedge while internal coil capacity is expanded (not a long-term strategy). Memphis overhead impacted Oklahoma segment margin by $9.8 million (29.6% excluding it vs 26.3% reported). Pricing actions are embedded in backlog.
quarterly_data.figure: Memphis overhead impact $9.8 million; Oklahoma margin 29.6% ex-Memphis vs 26.3% reported

quarterly_data.signal: BASX demand is broad-based across the portfolio: continued strength in traditional air-side products, liquid cooling CDUs (both liquid-to-air and liquid-to-liquid), and growing interest in AI-centric free cooling chillers designed to run at higher fluid temps supporting AI workloads. Orders come from existing customers plus new customers, and management is intentionally diversifying the customer base to reduce concentration risk.
